newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Finland leads in implementing EU social laws.
newsitem.headline: Finland leads in implementing EU social laws.

text.p: Finland is the only European Union country with a perfect record in implementing EU social policy laws, a survey released by the European Commission on Tuesday showed.
However Britain -- which opposes an active EU role in the social sector -- is not far behind, with a score of 96 percent.

Spain, on the other hand, is at the bottom of the list. It has turned into national law only 36 of 50 directives in areas such as labour law, worker health and safety and equal treatment between men and women, the Commission said.
Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn threatened to take slow-moving governments to court if they did not improve their records, citing Belgium, Spain and Ireland.
He warned that Spain could be subject to fines since the European Court of Justice had already ruled against it for failing to implement six health and safety measures.

The scores for the 15 EU member states are as follows: Austria (89.7), Belgium (82), Britain (96), Denmark (96), Finland (100), France (90), Germany (96), Greece (82), Ireland (85.7), Italy (78), Luxembourg (85.7), Netherlands (94), Portugal (81.6), Spain (72), Sweden (96).
Britain won an exemption from some social legislation in the 1992 Maastricht treaty, but it was covered by all but one of the directives included in the survey.
